title: SIU clears police officers in the fatal shooting of a Toronto man under investigation in the murder of his ex-girlfriend
subtitle: Gedi Ali Gedi, 46, rushed officers with a knife and cleaver as they investigated the suspected homicide of 32-year-old Amanda Killeen.
article: The SIU has cleared two officers in the death of a Toronto man during a homicide investigation.
In the early hours of Feb. 23, Toronto police Emergency Task Force officers were called to an apartment complex on 291 George St., to assist with a search warrant as part of a homicide investigation.
A 46-year-old man, identified as Gedi Ali Gedi rushed at them with a knife and cleaver as they were entering a unit, the SIU said.
The officers fired their guns and Gedi was struck. He was taken to hospital where he died.
Gedi was the ex-boyfriend and a person of interest in the case of 32-year-old Amanda Killeen, who was last seen on Feb. 19. Her remains were later found and identified.
Orson York, 59, of Toronto was also charged with accessory after the fact to murder and indignity to a human body.
The SIU concluded that the officers' actions were justified, considering their situation.
"The officers also would have known that Mr. Gedi was tied to a recent murder, and was willing and able to resort to extreme violence," says SIU director, Joseph Martino in a statement.

"In the circumstances, faced with an armed individual running in their direction from no more than a few metres away, I am unable to reasonably conclude that either of SO #2 or SO #1 acted with excessive force in meeting the lethal threat presented by Mr. Gedi with lethal threat of their own."
The SIU is an independent government agency that investigates the conduct of officials that may have resulted in death, serious injury, sexual assault and/or the discharge of a firearm at a person.
